title and abstract.summary: The study analyzed historical records of plant species and Orthoptera (grasshoppers and crickets) to test how nitrogen deposition and plant richness changes influenced the patterns of richness change of Orthoptera, considering their functional traits.

introduction.summary: The study investigated the relationships between Orthoptera species richness, plant species richness, and nitrogen deposition levels using data from the Netherlands.

results.summary: The study measured changes in species richness for Orthoptera and plants across different time periods and spatial scales in the Netherlands, examining relationships with ammonia deposition and food specialization. The study measured changes in species richness and related traits for the group Orthoptera across different spatial scales and environmental conditions.

discussion.summary: The study measured Orthoptera species richness across different time periods and levels of nitrogen deposition, and examined the relationship between Orthoptera species richness and plant species richness. The study examined the responses of different groups of Orthoptera based on their food traits (herbivores vs. non-herbivores) to changes in ammonia levels and plant species richness across various spatial scales.
